body: Since parsing and sanitizing are tightly coupled in the current APIs this is no longer a concern.
There's renewed interest in streaming parsing APIs so we should probably keep this open for v2.

> There's renewed interest in streaming parsing APIs so we should probably keep this open for v2.

This was briefly discussed in yesterday's meeting. Generally, this looks good to me. Some initial opinions, without having thought this through:

* The present Sanitizer design is very HTML-parser-adjacent. It should be easy to apply it to whatever the HTML parser produces, in whatever granularity.
* Sanitizer looks at one node at a time; Elements and its attributes are considered together. There are no decisions that take several nodes into account. That should make it easy to apply Sanitizer to sub-trees or partial trees.
* The replaceWithChildren action does need to know its children. The decision is node-local, but the action itself requires that the node 'knows' its children. The 'driver loop' wants to know about templates and shadow hosts in order to recurse into them. This would likely need to be taken into account.
* The API was a bit unclear to me; but I'll guess if there's an option bag somewhere it could contain a SanitizerConfig. I wonder if it'd make sense to have safe/unsafe variants.

Sanitizer API with streaming was discussed in a meeting today.

The proposed model is that the decisions are made based on the sanitizer config right before a nodes is inserted into the destination document. Before that point there can be no side effects, such as starting to load images. This should be covered by the fact that https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#html-fragment-parsing-algorithm uses a temporary inactive document, so even steps that are run at node creation time wouldn't happen since the node document is inactive.

`replaceWithChildren` would work by keeping track of elements that were not inserted into a document but should be replaced by its children. When a node is inserted into such an element (or is about to be inserted) it would be inserted at the destination insertion point instead. @zcorpan you mentioned that some HTML parser changes may be needed, would that be in support of `replaceWithChildren` specifically?

Another conrer case that has bypassed sanitizers in the past is the maximum nesting depth of 512 elements.
When fragment parsing, you start at 0 and not the nesting depth of the current element, but it still matters:
After receiving an element at the depth of 512, all new elements are created as siblings, rather than children.

This is how I see streaming support (half normative, half handwavy):

- First create the element in the inert document to avoid creation side effects like image fetching.
- The following applies *after* all of the other insertion-location adjustments:

```bikeshed

To <dfn>potentially parser-insert a node</dfn> |child| into [=node=] |parent|, given [=node=] |context| 
  and {{SanitizerConfig}} |config|:
  1. Let |ancestor| be |parent|.
  2. Assert: |parent| is |context| or somewhere below |context| in the stack of open elements.
  3. While |ancestor| is not |context|:
      1. Let |ancestorName| be a {{SanitizerElementNamespace}} with |ancestor|'s [=local name=] and [=namespace=].
      1. If |configuration|["replaceWithChildrenElements"] does not contain |ancestorName|, break.
      1. Set |ancestor| to the next element above |ancestor| in the [=stack of open items=].
  4. If |child| implements {{DocumentType}}, then insert |child| into |ancestor| and return.
  5. If |child| implements {{Text}}, then insert |child| into |ancestor| and return.
  6. If |child| implements {{Comment}}:
     1. If |configuration|["comments"] is true, then insert |child| into |ancestor|.
     1. Return.
   
  7. Let |elementName| be a {{SanitizerElementNamespace}} with |child|'s [=local name=] and [=namespace=].  
  8. If any of the following is true:
     * |configuration|["replaceWithChildrenElements"] contains |elementName|;
     * |configuration|["elements"] exists and does not [=map/contains=] |elementName|; or
     * |configuration|["removeElements"] [=map/contains=] |elementName|, 

     then return.

  9. Fix up the attributes for |child| as per existing algorithm.
  10. Insert |child| to |ancestor|.
 ```

The main consideration here is that the sanitizer decision happens *right at the end*, after all the structural parser adjustments like foster/adoption etc.

This ensures that the streaming sanitizer works the same way as the non-streaming one, which removes elements *after* parser fixups. For example, this can still remove `<tr>` elements which would result in `<tbody><td>`, just like the current sanitizer algorithm (to respond to https://github.com/WICG/sanitizer-api/issues/190#issuecomment-4659347365).

In addition to enforcing sanitizer decisions when [inserting](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#insert-a-foreign-element) elements, we also need to look at code paths that append directly and don't go through the insertion location adjustment machinery.

Looking at [create an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) call sites, here's what I found:
- The ["before html" insertion mode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-before-html-insertion-mode) creates and appends an `<html>` element to the document.
- The ["in head" insertion mode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#parsing-main-inhead) has a bunch of special handling of `<script>` elements that inserts without reference to an algorithm at step 6.
- The [adoption agency algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#adoption-agency-algorithm) creates and appends nodes.
- [Parsing XML documents](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#parsing-xhtml-documents), not sure if sanitizer can apply to XML parsing?
FYI I've prototyped the algorithm in https://github.com/WICG/sanitizer-api/issues/190#issuecomment-4659347416 in blink and it seems to do the right thing (though obviously needs lots of tests etc).
